mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate near zero indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces discount rates for equity valuation and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remains below 0.25% for 3 consecutive months and S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in >60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 7.0% signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls below 7.0%, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in >60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts and retail sales indicates robust consumer demand, which supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS rise by >0.5% in the past month, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in >60% of such cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production growth signals expanding manufacturing output and economic activity, which correlates with positive S&P 500 returns over a 60-day horizon.
failure_condition: In the industrial expansion phase (INDPRO growth rate > 0.5% monthly), S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in >60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL reading above 2.0% indicates rising inflation, which may trigger monetary tightening and reduce equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL rises above 2.0%, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in >60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Positive month-over-month growth in nonfarm payrolls indicates a strengthening labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS growth rate is positive, S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in >60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) and stagnant monetary policy (FEDFUNDS) signal potential monetary tightening, which pressures equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL rises and FEDFUNDS remains below 0.25%, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in >60% of such cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts below 550.0 thousand units indicates weakening residential demand, which may signal broader economic softness and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST falls below 550.0, S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in >60% of such instances.
